description: WHEN OTHER of 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT at :809-816, the THIRD and last arm of the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :786, whose WHEN order - NORMAL at :787, NOTFND at :789, OTHER at :809 - is preserved exactly (gate G30). The folder pins nine read outcomes across three call sites with no two cases overlapping (gate G47): case03 drives all three reads to NORMAL, case08 the 9200 NOTFND and case09 the 9200 WHEN OTHER at :759 on the CXACAIX path, case10 the 9300 NOTFND at :789 and THIS FILE the 9300 WHEN OTHER at :809 on ACCTDAT, case12 the 9400 NOTFND at :839 and case13 the 9400 WHEN OTHER at :858 on CUSTDAT. This file is the only one that pins the 9300 WHEN OTHER arm, so removing or re-pointing it would leave that arm undriven. Path: EIBCALEN 172 - the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy plus the 12-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :213, which :288-292 splits out of DFHCOMMAREA - with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM COCRDLIC, so the guard at :282-293 takes its ELSE and copies the inbound area rather than INITIALIZEing it; EIBAID DFHENTER satisfies :307-308 so the invalid-key remap at :312-314 leaves it alone; the main EVALUATE TRUE at :323-383 reaches its third arm WHEN CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :361, whose WHEN order - PFK03 at :324, ENTER at :353, REENTER at :361, OTHER at :375 - is preserved exactly (gate G30); 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT takes its ELSE, moving CC-ACCT-ID to CDEMO-ACCT-ID and setting FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID, so INPUT-ERROR is false at :364 and the ELSE at :368-373 performs 9000-READ-ACCT, then 1000-SEND-MAP, then GO TO COMMON-RETURN, which bypasses the trailing IF INPUT-ERROR at :387-392 and reaches :394 - a forward-only GO TO reproduced as a plain return with its evaluation order and fall-through outcome intact (rule R7). WHY THIS ARM IS FORCED RATHER THAN SEEDED, stated plainly: a WHEN OTHER is a file error, and no seeded or withheld row can produce one. Withholding the account row yields DFHRESP(NOTFND), which is a DIFFERENT arm and is case10's subject; measured over the whole fixtures, every XREF-ACCT-ID in cardxref.txt has a matching acctdata.txt row and every XREF-CUST-ID a matching custdata.txt row, so neither a miss nor an error is reachable from the unmodified data. ACCTDAT is therefore DECLARED EMPTY - a positive statement that a real 300-byte CVACT01Y dataset was opened and held no row, which is not the same assertion as omitting it - and the forced outcome is applied to the read of that empty dataset, which is what names WHICH of the three identically keyed READ sites the outcome lands on. CCXREF and CUSTDAT still hold their rows, so the flow still reaches the site being driven. This is case09's technique applied to the second site. 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT SUCCEEDS FIRST on the '00' outcome (gate G47), which is what proves the outcome is applied to one site rather than to every read: :739-740 move XREF-CUST-ID 000000050 and XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740 into the commarea. The three seeded cross-reference rows carry accounts 50, 27 and 2, so the finder must discriminate on its key rather than return the only row present, and cardxref.txt is ordered by card number rather than by account, which is why the account this case asks for sits at zero-based row 0 with its XREF-ACCT-ID span at offset 25 for 11 bytes. CXACAIX is a PATH over the CCXREF base, reached through the one CardXrefRepository's alternate-key finder and never through a second repository or a second table (gate G45) - a rule that holds on a failing path exactly as it does on a succeeding one. The guard at :696-699, whose original condition on :696 is itself commented out in favour of the flag test on :697, does not fire. 9300 then reads DATASET(LIT-ACCTFILENAME), which is PIC X(8) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' at :184-185 with its trailing space part of the value, RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) at 11 bytes, KEYLENGTH 11, INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD), LENGTH 300 - and reports the file error. The arm body, in source order: :810 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE, :811 SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE, :812 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME, :813 MOVE LIT-ACCTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE, :814 and :815 the two response codes, and :816 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG. The WS-LONG-MSG comment at :817 and the PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT at :818 stay commented out, as does the direct MOVE CUST-SSN at :495 that the hyphenating STRING at :496-504 replaced (practice B5). THE MESSAGE COMPOSITION, and the contrast that makes it worth pinning. WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is built at :86-105 from nine spans summing to exactly 80: FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ', ERROR-OPNAME X(8) holding 'READ', FILLER X(4) ' on ', ERROR-FILE X(9) holding LIT-ACCTFILENAME, FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ', ERROR-RESP X(10), FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ', ERROR-RESP2 X(10), and a closing FILLER X(5) of spaces - 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 re-sums as 80. MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG at :816 truncates that group into PIC X(75) at :117, and because a COBOL alphanumeric receiver truncates on the RIGHT it loses exactly the closing five-space FILLER and NOTHING ELSE - only padding goes. That is precisely the difference from the NOTFND arms, whose STRING is assembled rather than moved: 9400's at :846-856 sums 'CustId:' 7 + WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X 9 + ' not found' 10 + ' in customer master.Resp: ' 26, with a full stop and a TRAILING SPACE + ERROR-RESP 10 + ' REAS:' 6, in UPPER CASE unlike this program's other ' Reas:' at :802 + ERROR-RESP2 10, which re-sums as 7+9+10+26+10+6+10 = 78 into the same PIC X(75), so three bytes of REAL DATA are discarded from ERROR-RESP2's tail. :532 then moves the surviving 75 characters into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), re-padding by exactly 3, which is why the expected image measures 78 and ends in three spaces. The two response codes are not case data and cannot drift: a keyed read of an empty account dataset reports a file status with no CICS RESP to report, so FileStatus.RESP_NOT_REPORTED renders through respNotReportedImage as NINE ASTERISKS, and RESP2 is FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE = 0 rendering as nine digits; each is left justified in PIC X(10) with one pad space, giving '********* ' and '000000000 ', and both are compile-time constants (practice B7). The asterisks are the stronger assertion and not a cosmetic detail: the cross-reference repository DOES surface a CICS RESP for its own WHEN OTHER, which is why case09's message carries 000000019, so a translation that invented a zero for an unreported code would print 000000000 here and pass a weaker check. THE DEAD GUARD, and why the flow continues. :704-706 reads IF DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT. That 88-level sits on WS-RETURN-MSG at :131-132 with VALUE 'Did not find this account in account master file', and this arm wrote the file-error text instead, so the condition is FALSE and the guard NEVER FIRES - the same always-false shape the NOTFND arm reaches by a different route, since the SET that would have made it true is itself commented out at :792. Execution therefore CONTINUES: :708 moves CDEMO-CUST-ID into WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID and :710-711 perform 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST, which reads DATASET(LIT-CUSTFILENAME), PIC X(8) VALUE 'CUSTDAT ' at :188-189, with a 9-byte RIDFLD, KEYLENGTH 9 and LENGTH 500, finds customer 000000050 and takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :837-838, setting FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER. So FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is set on a path whose ACCOUNT read failed. This is reproduced, not repaired (practice B5): a case that expected an early exit here would be asserting a program this repository does not contain. The guard at :713-715 is likewise permanently false because its SET at :842 is commented out, immaterial only because 9400 is the last read. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, and the exact mirror of case12. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS takes its ELSE at :464 because EIBCALEN is 172, and with FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK false :468 echoes the typed CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO. Its guard at :471-472 is FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER OR FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER - OR, not AND - and although THIS case's account read failed, the customer flag is set, so the ten account moves at :473-490 DO run, over an ACCOUNT-RECORD that no read ever filled. COPY CVACT01Y at :244 is its own 01 group and is not among the three areas INITIALIZE names at :268-270, so it holds its allocated state, which the codec builds with COBOL INITIALIZE category defaults: alphanumeric spans spaces, numeric spans zeros. ACSTTUSO is therefore one space; ADTOPENO, AEXPDTO - :488 moves ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE and the copybook's misspelling is preserved verbatim - AREISDTO and AADDGRPO are ten spaces each; and the five PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 receivers at :475-485 render '+           .00': the sign is forced, all nine Z positions are suppressed because the integer part is zero and both commas are blanked with them, and the two decimals are still present because the mask ends .99 and not .ZZ - 15 characters, the LENGTH the mapset declares. case12 is the converse and the pair to this file: there the account read succeeds and the customer read misses, so the account items carry real data and the eighteen customer items stay LOW-VALUES. Here :493-523 populates all EIGHTEEN customer items from the real row, with the width-driven truncations the fixtures force: ACSZIPCO PIC X(5) keeps '04257' of CUST-ADDR-ZIP PIC X(10), ACSPHN1O and ACSPHN2O PIC X(13) each drop two characters of a PIC X(15) source, ACSTSSNO is the :496-504 STRING '931-24-8469' laid into a PIC X(12) item whose twelfth byte STRING leaves as the LOW-VALUES :432 put there, and the field the screen labels City is fed from CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 at :513. THE HIGHLIGHT, stated in BOTH directions so neither half reads as an omission. 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS moves DFHBMFSE into ACCTSIDA at :543, takes the EVALUATE at :546-552 whose three arms have IDENTICAL bodies - both WHENs and WHEN OTHER all move -1 into ACCTSIDL, and the redundancy is left exactly as written (practice B5) - colours the field DFHDFCOL at :555, and THEN OVERWRITES IT WITH DFHRED at :557-559 because this arm set FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :811. The asterisk at :561-565 stays away because it needs FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK, which 2210's ELSE cleared: RED WITHOUT THE MARKER, which is FieldAttributeSetter's rule, implemented inline here because COACTVWC does not copy CSSETATY (gate G38). The negative half belongs to the customer-side failures and is worth naming here so the difference is legible: 9400 sets FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK at :841 and at :860 - the CUSTOMER flag, not the account flag - so on those paths the IF at :557 does NOT fire and ACCTSIDC stays at the DFHDFCOL of :555 even though an error message is displayed. case12 and case13 pin that half; this file pins the half where the ACCOUNT flag is the one set, and the two together are what make gate G38 a pair rather than a single assertion. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR at :570 rather than the DFHBMDAR of :568 because :528-530 flipped WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE, set at :689, to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT before :567 tested it, which is also why INFOMSGO carries the prompt of :113-114 - a literal of exactly 40 characters, counted, which fills WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) with no padding of its own and then gains five trailing spaces on the way into INFOMSGO PIC X(45). Every xxxH item stays DFHDFHI because the program writes no extended highlight, and the programmed-symbol and validation planes are never written at all. 1400-SEND-SCREEN moves LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP at :579-580 and SETs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :581, so the reply names COACTVW, CACTVWA and context 1, and CDEMO-CUST-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM are populated from the successful 9200, unlike the cross-reference failure cases where they stay zeros; COMMON-RETURN at :394-407 is an EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CAVW') carrying the whole area, so the entire conversation - AID, commarea and screen values - travels in the payload with no server-side session state (gate G37, rule R6). COACTVWC writes nothing - its only file verbs are the three EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826 - so expectedWrites is empty as a POSITIVE assertion and expectedReturnCode is 0: an online file error builds a message and paints a screen, and the program contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD', so neither an abend nor a non-zero status is asserted anywhere (gate G35 does not apply). All four seeded rows are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel BOTH field by field AND as whole record images: three cross-reference rows at the 50 bytes CVACT03Y declares, normalised from the fixture's own 36 by CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 with the trailing FILLER X(14) as 14 spaces (gate G16, risk R-F), and one customer row at the 500 CVCUS01Y declares with its FILLER X(168) space filled (gates G19 and G21). Every field map covers 100 per cent of its record's bytes, FILLER included, so the diff is field-for-field rather than a single string comparison (gate G17) while the accompanying image proves the total width and therefore that every FILLER was emitted at all. ACCTDAT is pinned at rowCount 0 and recordLength 300 on the dataset channel, which is the only way to assert that a real dataset was opened and stayed empty - an empty expectedWrites list cannot distinguish that from never opening it. The two composed texts are carried in ERRMSGO and INFOMSGO rather than in expectedMessages, because the message channel of this harness records only SEND-PLAIN-TEXT at :877-887, whose EXEC CICS SEND TEXT and bare EXEC CICS RETURN a path that paints a map never reaches; an entry there would assert an emission this path does not make. PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the COBOL - 9300 at :776-820 and its WHEN OTHER arm at :809-816, WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE at :86-105, the always-false guard at :704-706 against the 88 at :131-132, 9400 at :826-870 including the MOVEs at :843-844 that sit BEFORE the IF at :845 where 9300 puts them inside it at :793-795, and 1200's OR at :471-472 - cross-checked against the 300-byte CVACT01Y, 50-byte CVACT03Y and 500-byte CVCUS01Y layouts including their FILLER spans, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY, the PICOUT masks of app/bms/COACTVW.bms and the real app/data/ASCII fixtures, which were measured rather than assumed: all 50 cross-reference rows are 36 bytes and all 50 customer rows are 500. None of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, which this environment cannot run (risk R-A). The images are US-ASCII, the clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:12:32 so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:12:32 rather than sampled (practice B7), and TITLE01O comes from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:19 with TITLE02O from its ACTIVE :22, :21 being commented out.
